paper.title: Be More Diverse than the Most Diverse: Optimal Mixtures of Generative Models via Mixture-UCB Bandit Algorithms

settings.name_in_paper: Mixture multi-armed bandit with quadratic loss (online selection of optimal mixtures)
unmapped: Objective is the quadratic loss L(P_hat^(T)) = (1/T^2) sum_{s,t} kappa(x^(s),x^(t)) + (1/T) sum_t f(x^(t)) of the empirical distribution of all collected samples, compared with the best mixture of arms min_alpha L(alpha); comparator is the best mixture, not the best single arm
kappa is a bounded positive semidefinite kernel with values in [kappa_0,kappa_1], f bounded in [f_0,f_1]; samples x lie in an arbitrary space X
Algorithm uses the sensitivity Delta_L = 2 Delta_kappa + Delta_f and Delta_kappa (range bounds of kappa and f)
settings.definition_quote: At time $t=1,\ldots,T$, we choose and pull an arm $b^{(t)}\in[m]$ (i.e., generate a sample from model $b^{(t)}$), and obtain a sample $x^{(t)}$ from the distribution $P_{b^{(t)}}$. ... here we minimize the loss $L(\hat{P}^{(T)})$ which involve cross terms $\kappa(x^{(s)},x^{(t)})$ between samples at different rounds.

symbols.Delta_L: sensitivity of the loss, 2*Delta_kappa + Delta_f (ranges of kappa and f)

conditions: kappa positive semidefinite and bounded, f bounded

source.label: thm:alg_converge
source.quote: Suppose $m \ge 2$, $\beta\ge4$. Consider bounded quadratic loss function (\ref{eq:general_loss}) with $\kappa$ being positive semidefinite. Let $\hat{P}^{(T)}$ be the empirical distribution of the first $T\ge2$ samples $\mathbf{x}^{(T)}$ given by Mixture-UCB-CAB. Then the gap between the expected loss and the optimal loss is bounded by $\mathbb{E}[L(\hat{P}^{(T)})]-\min_{\boldsymbol{\alpha}}L(\boldsymbol{\alpha}) \le4\Delta_{L}\sqrt{\frac{\beta m\log T}{T}}$.

results.notes: Paper's bound is on the average per-round (quadratic) regret; multiplied by T here. Paper's m = number of arms K. Quantity is a quadratic generalisation of regret against best mixture (reduces to pseudo-regret when kappa=0), hence 'other'. Proof gives improved constant 3.382. Algorithm's confidence widths use log t, not T, so recorded as anytime.
